note: Guides only: the kit never runs, installs or configures these. `kit plan/install --manual NAME` prints the steps and risks; a person decides and runs them. Rules: kit/mcp_catalog.py load_manual.

claude-code-router.summary: local gateway that sends Claude Code requests to other model providers (07_SOURCES_EVALUATION U-23)
claude-code-router.network_egress: your prompts and code go to the providers you configure
claude-code-router.file_access: stores provider credentials in its own data folder (~/.claude-code-router, Windows %APPDATA%\claude-code-router)
steps: Read the risks above; the kit does not run any of this.
Install (Node.js 22+, global npm): npm install -g @musistudio/claude-code-router@3.1.3
Start the service and open its UI: ccr ui   (management UI http://127.0.0.1:3458, gateway http://127.0.0.1:3456)
In the UI add a provider and its API key, then create a Claude Code profile under Agent Config.
Run Claude Code through it: ccr "<profile-name>" cli
undo: ccr stop
npm uninstall -g @musistudio/claude-code-router
Delete its data folder if you no longer need the stored provider keys.

headroom.summary: context-compression proxy that wraps a coding agent and relays its model requests (07_SOURCES_EVALUATION U-08). An anonymous telemetry beacon is ON by default
headroom.network_egress: your model requests pass through its local proxy to the provider; anonymous beacon (compression ratios, provider and model IDs, OS) on by default; PyPI update check at most once a day
headroom.file_access: keeps originals for retrieval in its local store; `headroom wrap` registers itself with the wrapped agent until `headroom unwrap`
steps: Read the risks above; the kit does not run any of this.

Turn telemetry and update checks off first (README 'Telemetry'): set HEADROOM_TELEMETRY=off and HEADROOM_BEACON=off (or DO_NOT_TRACK=1, or HEADROOM_OFFLINE=1), and HEADROOM_UPDATE_CHECK=off, in the shell you start it from.
Install the pinned version in its own environment: uv tool install --python 3.13 "headroom-ai[all]==0.43.1"
Run one wrapped session: headroom wrap claude   (or: headroom wrap codex). The proxy exits with the wrapped agent.
undo: headroom unwrap claude   (and/or: headroom unwrap codex) removes a durable wrap or registration
uv tool uninstall headroom-ai
Unset the HEADROOM_* variables you set.

rtk.license: Apache-2.0 for the rtk-oss edition; the default rtk binary is Apache-2.0 + BUSL-1.1 and rtk-proxy is BUSL-1.1
rtk.summary: shell hook that rewrites the agent's Bash commands to compress their output (07_SOURCES_EVALUATION U-20). Use the Apache-2.0-only rtk-oss edition
rtk.network_egress: none for the hook; telemetry is off by default (opt in only with `rtk telemetry enable`)
rtk.file_access: `rtk init -g` writes a hook into the agent's user settings (Claude Code by default, `--codex` for Codex)
steps: Read the risks above; the kit does not run any of this. Pick rtk-oss: the default rtk binary mixes Apache-2.0 and BUSL-1.1, and both editions install a binary named rtk, so only one can be installed.
Install rtk-oss 1.1.0 from the release binaries or the methods in the installation guide (https://www.rtk-ai.app/guide/getting-started/installation); on macOS/Linux: brew install rtk-ai/tap/rtk-oss
Preview with the --dry-run option the Quick Start guide describes, then add the hook: rtk init -g   (Codex: rtk init -g --codex)
Restart the agent.
undo: Remove the hook with the uninstall step of the Quick Start guide (https://www.rtk-ai.app/guide/getting-started/quick-start); the kit did not verify its exact flag.
Uninstall the binary the same way you installed it (for example: brew uninstall rtk-oss).
Restart the agent.

graphify.summary: code knowledge-graph CLI and skill; installs a PreToolUse hook (Claude Code) or instruction blocks (AGENTS.md for Codex) that steer the agent to the graph (07_SOURCES_EVALUATION U-07). PyPI name is graphifyy (two y)
graphify.network_egress: PyPI download; extraction uses your agent or the backends you configure with API keys; README says no telemetry
graphify.file_access: reads the repository; writes graphify-out/, a PreToolUse hook and CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md instructions; `graphify hook install` adds git hooks
steps: Read the risks above; the kit does not run any of this.
Install the pinned CLI: uv tool install graphifyy==0.9.104
Register it for this project only (not user-wide): graphify install --project   (Codex: graphify install --project --platform codex)
In the agent: /graphify .
undo: graphify uninstall   (add --purge to also delete graphify-out/)
If you ran graphify hook install, remove those git hooks too (see the docs).
uv tool uninstall graphifyy

claude-mem.summary: session memory: hooks capture tool activity, a local worker summarises it and later sessions recall it (07_SOURCES_EVALUATION U-42). Usage analytics are ON by default; the installer auto-installs Bun and uv
claude-mem.network_egress: npm download; anonymous usage analytics on by default; the memory provider you choose (claude-mem observer service, OpenRouter/Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan); optional browser sign-in and cloud sync
claude-mem.file_access: stores session observations in ~/.claude-mem; registers hooks and a plugin with each agent it sets up; installs Bun and uv if missing
steps: Read the risks above; the kit does not run any of this. Session content is stored and summarised.
To skip the account sign-in, set CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false (or pass an explicit --provider).
Install the pinned version in an interactive terminal: npx claude-mem@15.12.0 install   (it asks which agents; --ide values: npx claude-mem@15.12.0 --help)
Turn analytics off: npx claude-mem@15.12.0 telemetry disable
undo: Uninstall is only partly documented upstream (README at the pinned commit has no uninstall section); the kit does not invent the missing steps.
In Claude Code remove the plugin from /plugin; check the agent's settings for hooks it added.
Delete ~/.claude-mem if you no longer want the stored memory.
Bun and uv that it installed stay; remove them separately if you do not use them.

openrig.summary: tmux-based multi-agent rigs (07_SOURCES_EVALUATION U-10). No native Windows: macOS, Linux or WSL2 only. Its setup writes ~/.codex and ~/.claude
openrig.network_egress: npm download; may install tmux, Herdr and a missing Claude Code or Codex during `rig setup`
openrig.file_access: `rig setup` and its daemon write ~/.tmux.conf, ~/.openrig, hooks and trust in ~/.codex/config.toml, workspace trust in ~/.claude.json, hooks in the project's .claude/settings.local.json, and skills in ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills
steps: Read the risks above; the kit does not run any of this. Use macOS, Linux or WSL2 (native Windows is not supported).
Install the pinned CLI (Node.js 22 or 24): npm install -g @openrig/cli@0.7.9   (its postinstall only checks Node.js and SQLite)
Preview what setup changes: rig setup --dry-run --providers claude   (or codex)
Apply it: rig setup --providers claude --no-herdr
undo: Uninstall is only partly documented upstream (the README lists what setup changes but gives no uninstall command); the kit does not invent the missing steps.
npm uninstall -g @openrig/cli

Remove the OpenRig block from ~/.tmux.conf, its hooks and trust entries from ~/.codex/config.toml, its hooks from .claude/settings.local.json, and its skills (openrig-skills, refocusing, rigs) from ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills.
Delete ~/.openrig.

ruflo.summary: orchestration platform: MCP server, hooks, background daemon and swarms (07_SOURCES_EVALUATION U-44). Upstream examples use @latest; pin 3.72.2 yourself
ruflo.network_egress: npm download; whatever model providers and federation you configure
ruflo.file_access: `ruflo init` writes .claude/, .claude-flow/, CLAUDE.md, helpers and settings into the project and starts hooks and a daemon
steps: Read the risks above; the kit does not run any of this.
Smallest surface (MCP only, Claude Code's default local scope): claude mcp add ruflo -- npx -y ruflo@3.72.2 mcp start
Full CLI setup (writes the project files listed above): npx -y ruflo@3.72.2 init
undo: claude mcp remove ruflo

Uninstall after `init` is only partly documented upstream; the kit does not invent the missing steps. Use git status / git diff to find and remove the files it added (.claude/, .claude-flow/, CLAUDE.md changes, settings) and stop its daemon.

bureau-des-agents.summary: local web 'office' UI that runs and shows Claude Code agents (07_SOURCES_EVALUATION U-45). Interface in French
bureau-des-agents.network_egress: git clone and npm install; the agents it starts use your Claude Code account; the server listens on 127.0.0.1 only
bureau-des-agents.file_access: its clone folder; the agents it starts work in the folders you give them
steps: Read the risks above; the kit does not run any of this. Needs Node.js 22.18+ and a signed-in Claude Code.
git clone https://github.com/devlikemasta/bureau-des-agents.git, then cd bureau-des-agents and git checkout 184daa898cbb
npm install   (dependency install scripts were not reviewed by the kit)
npm start, then open http://localhost:4848
undo: Stop the server (Ctrl+C in its terminal).
Delete the cloned bureau-des-agents folder.

mobbin.summary: remote MCP (Streamable HTTP, OAuth) with Mobbin's app screens and flows (U-35). Remote servers never go into catalog/mcp.json (§15); you add it yourself
mobbin.network_egress: every tool call goes to https://api.mobbin.com/mcp with your OAuth session
mobbin.file_access: none; Claude Code stores the OAuth session itself
steps: Read the risks above; the kit does not run any of this. No API key: sign-in is OAuth in the browser.
claude mcp add --transport http mobbin https://api.mobbin.com/mcp   (Mobbin's page uses --scope user; without it the server is added for this project only)
In Claude Code run /mcp and sign in to Mobbin.
undo: claude mcp remove mobbin
Revoke the access in your Mobbin account if you no longer use it.

nicelydone.summary: remote MCP (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration) with SaaS screens and flows (U-36). The command below is Claude Code's generic form: Nicelydone shows its own wording only after sign-in (UNVERIFIED)
nicelydone.network_egress: every tool call goes to https://mcp.nicelydone.club/mcp with your OAuth session
nicelydone.file_access: none; Claude Code stores the OAuth session itself
steps: Read the risks above; the kit does not run any of this. No API key: sign-in is OAuth.
claude mcp add --transport http nicelydone https://mcp.nicelydone.club/mcp
In Claude Code run /mcp and sign in to Nicelydone.
undo: claude mcp remove nicelydone
Revoke the access in your Nicelydone account if you no longer use it.

refero.license: Refero terms of service (Pro plan includes MCP tool calls)
refero.summary: remote MCP (HTTP) with product screens and user flows (U-37). Use OAuth: the docs also show an Authorization header with a token, which would put a secret into the MCP config, so this guide leaves it out
refero.network_egress: every tool call goes to https://api.refero.design/mcp with your OAuth session
refero.file_access: none; Claude Code stores the OAuth session itself
steps: Read the risks above; the kit does not run any of this.
claude mcp add --transport http refero https://api.refero.design/mcp   (sign in with OAuth; do not add a token header)
In Claude Code run /mcp and complete the sign-in.
undo: claude mcp remove refero
Revoke the access in your Refero account if you no longer use it.
